page: Microsoft Azure E16ds_v7 is an Edsv7-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The physical layout consists of 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes an L3 cache of 480 MB, alongside L1d and L2 caches of 48 KB and 2 MB respectively. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

This server configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, which positions it within the memory-optimized class. Local storage is provided via a bundled 945 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No public IPv4 addresses are included by default, and there are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute and memory tasks, with specific top-tier results in single-threaded operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests fall within the average category, as do the PassMark CPU and memory scores. However, single-threaded gzip compression (36.52 GB/sec) and single-threaded bzip3 decompression (15.37 GB/sec) reach top-tier levels. Large-block memory bandwidth is measured at 136.15 GB/sec for read operations and 56.03 GB/sec for write operations. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, text generation achieves a top-tier speed of 343.48 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16ds_v7 offers high memory density and a large L3 cache relative to its 16 vCPUs, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads without paying for excess compute cores. The combination of 128 GB RAM, 945 GB of local storage, and average database operation benchmarks makes this instance suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and data processing pipelines.
